jobs.title: Supply Chain Program Manager
jobs.description:
About Giga

Giga is building gigawatts of AI data centers to hasten a future of intelligence and abundance. We build data centers fast and at scale by combining the capabilities of an equipment supplier, engineering firm, general contractor, and real estate developer under one roof. Our team moves quickly and thinks practically. If you're ready to make an impact in an industry that matters, we're looking for people like you.

Why join Giga

The Pace: We're building at a speed most companies talk about but never actually operate at. If you've been bored somewhere else, you won't be here.
The Impact: Every person at Giga touches the work that matters. No layers, no waiting for approval chains. You'll see your fingerprints on what we ship.
The Team: A team of operators defining the future of AI infrastructure. We recruit A-players from the most innovative companies in the world, and they choose Giga because the work here means more.
The Moment: AI doesn't run without power, and that's us. Giga is the picks and shovels behind the AI revolution. This industry is about to explode, and you'll be in the room where it's already happening.

What You’ll Do

We're looking for a Supply Chain Program Manager
to sit at the center of our biggest, most complex programs and own them end to end: from the moment a design leaves engineering to the moment a unit ships and clears the customer's timeline.

This is not a coordination role. This is a single-threaded-owner role. You are the source of truth for program status, the person who knows exactly where every program stands at any moment, and the person who makes sure it doesn't stall — regardless of which function is holding the ball. If materials are missing, you know why and what's being done. If a design change lands, you know what it touches and who needs to move. If a supplier slips, you're already on the call. You report facts, not vibes, and you close gaps before they become headlines.

We're looking for someone who has operated in high-velocity, high-consequence manufacturing environments where the standard is total ownership, relentless attention to detail, and the willingness to personally chase down whatever is blocking the program.

Where you’ll work

We are an in-office culture — velocity matters when you're building physical infrastructure, and the best decisions happen in the room. This role is ideally based in our Long Beach, or Houston
offices, with full-time onsite expectations outside of bi-weekly WFH Fridays.

Responsibilities

Program Leadership, End to End

You are the single point of accountability and you own the full program lifecycle for assigned programs — from design freeze through materials procurement, production, quality release, and shipment to the customer.
Build and maintain master program schedules (Gantt-based) integrating design milestones, procurement lead times, production slots, quality gates, and shipping/logistics — and keep them alive, not static slideware.
Run the cadence: daily/weekly program stand-ups, cross-functional syncs, and executive-level status reporting, tailored to the audience but always grounded in the same source of truth.

Cross-Functional Orchestration

Sit at the intersection of materials, procurement, engineering/design changes, production scheduling, quality, logistics, and customer-facing timelines — and actively drive each function toward the program's critical path, not just track what they report.
Translate design changes into real operational impact in hours, not days: what does this ECN do to the BOM, the schedule, the supplier commitments, existing inventory, and the customer date — and who needs to act right now.
Identify the critical path continuously, not just at kickoff — re-sequence and re-prioritize as risks emerge.
Escalate early and precisely. You're expected to know a problem is coming before the function that owns it says the words out loud.

Execution & Timeline Management

Push urgency into every sub-function without owning their day-to-day work — you hold people to commitments, you don't do their job for them.
Drive material readiness, procurement PO status, and production slotting toward the customer commit date; flag and resolve conflicts between programs competing for the same constrained resources (capacity, long-lead components, engineering bandwidth).
Own risk management for the program: maintain a live risk register, quantify schedule/cost exposure, and drive mitigation — not just track that a risk "exists."

Customer & Stakeholder Management

Own the customer-facing delivery timeline and be the internal owner of what it will take to hit it — including saying "no" or "not by that date" with a credible alternative when needed.
Interface directly with customers on program status where required, translating internal complexity into a clear, confident external narrative.
Represent the program to executive leadership with concise, accurate, no-spin updates — you bring the real picture, including bad news, before it's asked for.

Negotiation & Influence

Negotiate priority, resources, and trade-offs across functions that don't report to you — procurement, engineering, production, quality, logistics — using data and relationships, not authority.
Resolve competing priorities between programs and functions by bringing facts, options, and a recommendation, not just an escalation.
Work directly with suppliers and contract manufacturers when a program-critical issue requires it, in coordination with procurement.

Requirements

Automotive, aerospace, or industrial equipment — ideally with direct exposure to hardware NPI or high-mix, high-complexity production environments.
Track record of owning complex, multi-function programs end to end in a fast-moving, high-consequence environment.
Deep comfort with the mechanics of a BOM, engineering change process, procurement lead times, and production scheduling — you don't need this explained to you twice.
Demonstrated ability to build and run master program schedules (MS Project, Smartsheet, or equivalent Gantt tooling) that people actually use to make decisions.
Strong technical fluency — able to read a drawing, understand a BOM, and have a credible conversation with engineering, quality, and manufacturing without a translator.
Proven negotiator — someone who gets functional leaders to move without formal authority over them, through credibility, data, and relentless follow-through.
High agency by default: you find the answer, you don't wait for it to be handed to you. You chase down the missing piece of information rather than reporting that it's missing.
Obsessive attention to detail combined with the judgment to know which details actually matter to the timeline.
Comfortable operating with imperfect information and lean support — this is a startup-paced environment inside a scaling industrial company, not a mature PMO.
Willingness to travel internationally (China, Mexico) as programs require. About 15-20%.

Pay Transparency

The range provided below is the role’s Base Salary range. This salary range may be inclusive of several career levels at Giga and will be narrowed during the interview process based on a number of factors, including the candidate’s experience and qualifications. Additional benefits include 401(k) plan plus subsidized medical, dental, and vision benefits.

Base Pay Range

$140,000 - $220,000 USD

How We Work

We value people who take ownership, raise risks early, communicate directly, and follow through. Incomplete information is part of the job. Make the best decision you can, document it, and adjust as the facts change. Move quickly on reversible decisions and take more care when security, safety, financial, employee, or customer risk is involved.

Benefits

Subsidized health, dental, and vision insurance
Equity (options) in a rapidly growing startup
401(k) with 4% employer match
Unlimited PTO
Parental leave
Healthcare and Dependent Care Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA) or Health Savings Account (HSA)
Commuter benefits, where applicable
Opportunities to collaborate in person at periodic team and company on-sites

Equal Opportunity Employer Statement

Giga Energy is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to fostering an inclusive and diverse workplace. We do not discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic as outlined by federal, state, or local laws. Giga Energy complies with all applicable labor laws, including the California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA) and other relevant state and federal regulations. jobs.title: CEO Office - Technical Project Manager (Mensch)
jobs.description:
Deine Mission & Herausforderungen

NEURA Robotics entwickelt die weltweit erste kognitive Robotik-Plattform – Roboter, die sehen, schlussfolgern und gemeinsam mit Menschen in Fabriken, Krankenhäusern und im eigenen Zuhause handeln können. Die nächsten drei Jahre werden darüber entscheiden, wer diese Kategorie weltweit anführt. Wir wollen dieses Unternehmen sein und die europäische Antwort in einem Wettbewerb geben, der derzeit von den USA und China dominiert wird.

Das CEO Office überträgt die Vision des CEOs in die Realität und beseitigt alles, was zwischen dem Unternehmen und seinem eingeschlagenen Kurs steht. Wir arbeiten eng mit dem CEO und dem Führungsteam an den Themen, die im jeweiligen Quartal am wichtigsten sind – mit der Geschwindigkeit und Qualität, die die jeweilige Situation erfordert.

In dieser Rolle übernimmst du Initiativen, die sich direkt aus der Vision des CEOs und der Unternehmensstrategie ableiten – Themen, die bestimmen, wohin sich NEURA als Nächstes entwickelt – mit einem klaren technischen Fokus auf unsere Produkte, Plattformen und die dahinterstehende Engineering-Organisation.

Das reicht von Produkt- und Technologie-Roadmaps, der Entwicklung von Business Cases für neue Produkte oder Spin-offs und der Gestaltung einer skalierbaren Organisation bis hin zu strategischen Partnerschaften, Markteintritten und dem Aufbau von Governance-Strukturen.

Gleichzeitig kümmerst du dich um kritische, zeit-sensitive Engpässe, die zwischen verschiedenen Funktionen entstehen und ein direktes Eingreifen des CEO Office erfordern – also um die Dinge, die in einem Unternehmen, das so schnell wächst, oft unbemerkt ins Stocken geraten.

In beiden Fällen übernimmst du die Verantwortung für das gesamte Thema: Du strukturierst das Problem, entwickelst den Weg nach vorn und bringst das Ergebnis erfolgreich ins Ziel – ohne vorgefertigten Fahrplan.

Konkret Bedeutet Das Für Dich

Du leitest strategische Initiativen, die das Unternehmen skalierbar machen – von der Definition bis zur Umsetzung. Dazu gehören langfristige Wachstumsstrategien, Produkt- und Technologie-Roadmaps, der Aufbau neuer Geschäftsbereiche und die Gestaltung der Organisation.
Du steuerst Produkt- und Technologiethemen mit einem klaren Mandat des CEOs. Du unterstützt unsere Business Units dabei, übergeordnete Produktvisionen in Roadmaps mit klaren Meilensteinen zu übersetzen. Gleichzeitig schaffst du Transparenz über Releases, Abhängigkeiten und Fortschritte, damit das Führungsteam fundierte Entscheidungen treffen kann.
Du entwickelst die Business Cases hinter den nächsten strategischen Schritten des Unternehmens – etwa für neue Produkte, Spin-offs, Expansionen in neue Länder, Partnerschaften oder M&A – und koordinierst die operativen, technischen, rechtlichen und organisatorischen Schritte, um diese Vorhaben zum Leben zu erwecken.
Du gewinnst einen direkten operativen Einblick in die Produktteams und steuerst sie strategisch. Du weißt aus erster Hand, wo die Teams stehen. Im engen Austausch mit dem CEO und dem Führungsteam bereitest du strategische Entscheidungen vor und diskutierst sie, schaffst Transparenz über Status, Risiken und Abhängigkeiten und stellst sicher, dass Entscheidungen tatsächlich in den Teams umgesetzt werden.
Du bist die Schnittstelle zwischen Strategie und Umsetzung – über Engineering, Product, Manufacturing, Marketing, Finance und People hinweg. Wenn ein Thema zwischen verschiedenen Funktionen liegt, übernimmst du es und bringst es voran. Dabei sprichst du die Sprache der Ingenieur genauso souverän wie die des Managements.
Du repräsentierst das CEO Office nach außen gegenüber Senior Partnern, Lieferanten, Investoren und Ansprechpartnern, wenn die Zeit des CEOs nicht ausreicht. Du triffst Entscheidungen, bleibst dran und sorgst dafür, dass Themen konsequent abgeschlossen werden.

Was du mitbringen solltest

Diese Rolle richtet sich an jemanden, der bereits Dinge aufgebaut und umgesetzt hat. Das CEO Office ist ein kleines Executive-Team, das im Auftrag des CEOs handelt – deshalb wählen wir unsere Teammitglieder sehr sorgfältig aus.

Wir suchen jemanden mit einem technischen Fundament und einer Erfolgsbilanz, bei der die Arbeit für sich selbst spricht. Entscheidend ist weniger dein bisheriger Jobtitel als das, was du bereits umgesetzt hast – und welchen Impact und welche Umsetzungskraft du künftig einbringen wirst.

Mindestens 5 Jahre Berufserfahrung im technischen Programm- oder Projektmanagement, in der Strategieberatung, im Corporate Development oder im Scale-up-Umfeld – idealerweise in den Bereichen Robotik, Maschinenbau oder Software/AI.
Technisches Verständnis. Du hast beispielsweise einen Abschluss in Wirtschaftsingenieurwesen, Engineering Management, Maschinenbau, Software Engineering oder einem vergleichbaren technischen Bereich – oder nachweislich tiefgehende Kenntnisse in Bereichen wie Software und AI, Systems Engineering, Mechatronik oder Fertigungsprozessen. Du verstehst Ingenieur, kannst ihre Ansätze kritisch hinterfragen und zwischen technischer Realität und unternehmerischen Entscheidungen übersetzen.
Nachweisbare Umsetzungskraft – von Anfang bis Ende. Du hast funktionsübergreifende strategische Initiativen von der Problemdefinition über die Umsetzung bis zum Ergebnis geführt – mit der Haltung eines Owners und nicht nach einer reinen Aufgaben-Checkliste. Menschen, die mit dir gearbeitet haben, würden dich als jemanden beschreiben, der Dinge umsetzt – nicht nur als jemanden, der sie koordiniert.
Erfahrung im Scale-up-Umfeld. Du warst bereits Teil eines Unternehmens, das schnell gewachsen ist, und weißt, an welchen Punkten es in den verschiedenen Wachstumsphasen typischerweise schwierig wird – bei Organisation, Prozessen, Talenten und Governance.
Starke analytische Fähigkeiten. Du verfügst über Erfahrung mit Financial Modelling, Business Cases, Marktanalysen und P&L-Denken. Du übersetzt Zahlen in Empfehlungen und Empfehlungen in konkrete Entscheidungen.
Souveräne Kommunikation auf Executive-Level und im Stakeholder-Management. Du erstellst präzise schriftliche Unterlagen, entscheidungsreife Analysen und Entscheidungsvorlagen. Gleichzeitig bewegst du dich souverän auf C-Level mit Executives, Investoren, Lieferanten und Senior Partnern über verschiedene Kulturen und Regionen hinweg – von Europa über die USA bis nach Asien.
Professionalität und gutes Urteilsvermögen. Du gehst verantwortungsvoll und diskret mit sensiblen Informationen um. Du bringst Ergebnisse – nicht unnötiges Aufsehen.
Sprachen. Verhandlungssicheres Englisch wird vorausgesetzt. Deutsch ist von Vorteil. Business-fließendes Deutsch und Englisch – beide Sprachen sind für diese Position erforderlich.

jobs.description:
Your mission & challenges

NEURA Robotics is building the world's first cognitive robotics platform — robots that can see, reason, and act alongside people in factories, hospitals, and homes. The next three years will decide who leads this category globally. We intend to be that company, and to be the European answer in a race currently dominated by the US and China.

The CEO Office transfers the CEO's vision into reality and unblocks whatever stands between the company and its trajectory. We work alongside the CEO and the leadership team on the topics that matter most in any given quarter, at the speed and quality the moment requires.

In this role, you take on the initiatives that derive directly from the CEO's vision and corporate strategy — the topics that define where NEURA goes next — with a clear technical anchor: our products, platforms, and the engineering organization behind them. This ranges from product and technology roadmaps, business case development for new products or spin-offs, and organizational design for scale, to strategic partnerships, market entries, and governance build-out. At the same time, you step in on the critical, time-sensitive bottlenecks that sit between functions and require direct CEO Office intervention — the things that break silently inside a company growing this fast. In both cases, you take work end-to-end: framing the problem, structuring the path forward, and landing the outcome without a playbook.

Concretely, This Means You Will

Lead strategic initiatives that scale the company — from definition through execution. Long-term growth strategy, product and technology roadmaps, new business setups, organizational design.
Steer product and technology topics with a CEO mandate — support our Business Units in breaking high-level product visions down into roadmaps with clear milestones, and create transparency on releases, dependencies, and progress for leadership decisions.
Build the business cases behind the company's next moves — new products, spin-offs, country expansions, partnerships, M&A — and coordinate the operational, technical, legal, and organizational steps to bring them to life.
Gain operational insight inside the product teams and guide them strategically — you know first-hand where the teams stand, and in close exchange with the CEO and the leadership team you prepare and discuss strategic decisions, create transparency on status, risks, and dependencies, and make sure decisions actually land in the teams.
Be the interface between strategy and execution — across Engineering, Product, Manufacturing, Marketing, Finance, and People. Where a topic sits between functions, you take it and move it — and you speak the language of engineers as fluently as that of the boardroom.
Represent the CEO Office externally with senior partners, suppliers, investors, and counterparts when the CEO's time doesn't scale. Decide, follow up, close the loop.

What We Can Look Forward To

This role is for someone who has already built things. The CEO Office is a small executive team acting on behalf of the CEO, and we hire carefully. We are looking for someone with a technical foundation and the kind of track record where the work argues for itself — less defined by a job title than by the work you have already done, and by the impact and execution you will bring going forward.

5+ years of experience in technical program/project management, strategy consulting, corporate development, or scale-up operations — ideally in robotics, machinery, or software/AI environments.
Technical fluency. A degree in, for example, industrial engineering, engineering management, mechanical engineering, software engineering, or a comparable technical field — or proven depth in areas such as software and AI, systems engineering, mechatronics, or manufacturing processes. You understand engineers, can challenge them, and translate between technical reality and business decisions.
Proven delivery, end-to-end. You have led cross-functional strategic initiatives from framing through execution to outcome — with an owner's instinct, not an employee's checklist. People you have worked with would describe you as someone who delivers, not someone who coordinates.
Scale-up operating experience. You have been inside a company growing fast and know where it breaks at each stage: organization, processes, talent, and governance.
Strong analytical foundation — financial modelling, business cases, market sizing, P&L thinking. You translate numbers into recommendations, and recommendations into decisions.
Executive communication and stakeholder fluency. Sharp written materials, board-ready analyses, decision-support memos — and you hold your own with C-level executives, investors, suppliers, and senior partners across cultures and geographies, from Europe to the US and Asia.
Professionalism and judgment. Sound discretion when handling sensitive information. You bring the work, not the noise.

jobs.title: Program Manager, Safety
jobs.description:
About Bolt

Bolt is shaping a future where cities are built for people, not cars. What started as an ambitious project of a 19-year-old in 2013 has grown into a global mobility platform used by more than 200 million customers and 4.5 million driver and courier partners across 50 countries.

From ride-hailing and food delivery to scooters, e-bikes, and car-sharing, Bolt helps people move through cities every day. Small, autonomous teams drive this work, combining the speed and ownership of a startup with the scale of a global technology company backed by more than €1bn in funding.

And we're just getting started.

Why join Bolt?

Build the future of mobility and help transform how people live and move in cities.
Tackle challenges at scale that span technology, operations, regulation, and growth.
Take real ownership early. Small, lean teams mean your decisions matter from day one, and you'll learn fast alongside some of the best people in the industry.
Join one of Europe's leading technology companies, backed by world-class investors including Sequoia.

About The Role

Our Central Safety team is responsible for monitoring and preventing risks that could cause real-world harm to users and accounts. In this role, you will oversee safety programs-related KPIs, analyze trends, coordinate prevention strategies for identified risks, and develop safety risk assessments for new projects and product updates. Our goal is to protect Bolt users globally, minimize reputational and safety risks, and support sustainable company growth.

Main Tasks And Responsibilities

Analyze safety risk trends, incidents, and crises to identify emerging risks, uncover root causes, and recommend preventive actions.
Collaborate with the Data Science team to validate and refine predictive models, enhancing detection and prevention of safety risks.
Develop, maintain, and optimize risk prevention products and processes to protect users and minimize financial and reputational impact.
Lead safety programs and coordinate cross-functionally with Product, Engineering, Local Operations, Customer Support, Public Policy, Marketing, Compliance, and other relevant stakeholders.
Provide expert consultation and guidance to ensure safety considerations are embedded across projects and operations.
Provide regular visibility into program metrics, initiatives, and progress against strategic goals.

About You

You have a proven experience in program management, with a focus on Trust & Safety, and/ or risk management.
You have strong collaboration skills, with experience working with cross-functional teams including engineering, data science, product, and legal.
You have excellent communication, problem-solving, and organizational skills.
You are able to manage multiple complex projects and adapt to evolving priorities.

Why you’ll love it here

Accelerate your professional growth with unique career opportunities.
Enjoy a rewarding salary and stock options, knowing that as Bolt succeeds, so do you.
Take care of your physical and mental health with our wellness perks.
Celebrate 5 years at Bolt with a 1-month paid sabbatical to recharge.
Connect with colleagues at annual company events and smaller team gatherings.

Kitchenaid Small Appliances (KASA)
is currently seeking qualified candidates for our Project Leadership Office (PLO) as Project/Program Manager. The role is based at our Global Head Quarters located in Michigan, US.

The Manager in the Project Leadership Office (PLO) leads cross-functional teams to deliver consumer relevant launches with speed, quality, and efficiency. The Project Manager drives the consistent application of the Whirlpool Product Development (WPD) system to enable disciplined execution and predictability, while enabling flexibility to meet consumer and business needs. Additionally, this role will act as a project leader for the KASA Test Kitchen, a strategic initiative to validate and de-risk new category entry into the small appliances space, ensuring that KASA can rapidly and systematically pursue its growth ambition.

Lead cross-functional project teams with clarity, ensuring accountability for scope, timing, cost, quality, consumer outcomes, and delivery against the business commitments.
Apply the Whirlpool Product Development process with discipline and judgment, coaching teams on stage-rigor, deliverables, and governance while tailoring execution to project risk and complexity.
Connect project execution to business outcomes by understanding the business case, defining success measures, and challenging assumptions when project decisions put expected consumers or business outcomes at risk.
Lead and operationalize early-stage Advanced Development Projects (ADP) to de-risk execution, comfortably operating 'in the grey' to orchestrate the team through validating desirability, feasibility, and viability before business case commitment.
Translate enterprise strategy and category priorities into actionable project plans, frame options, trade-offs, and recommendations to enable timely leadership decisions.
Anticipate risks, escalate with transparency, and drive resolution through data-based decisions.
Build strong followership by creating psychological safety, modeling straight talk, and empowering team members to take ownership.
Partner with category leaders, Marketing, Engineering, Brand and Operations to ensure launches are consumer-centric and business-viable.
Manage stakeholder relationships proactively—aligning cross-functional leaders, clarifying decision ownership, and ensuring transparency of status, risks, and trade-offs.
Continuously improve ways of working, leveraging Lean/CI methodologies to reduce waste and increase predictability.
Ability to travel 1-2 times per year to OEM supplier sites is required to provide on-site project oversight, conduct quality assurance and production reviews, and maintain strong working relationships at all critical project phases.

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Business, or related field
Proven experience leading cross-functional project teams within consumer product development or related industries.
Demonstrated expertise in structured product development processes (WPD or equivalent).
Strong stakeholder management and influencing skills, with proven ability to align diverse functions and geographies.
Demonstrated ability to navigate ambiguity, connect multiple sources of information, challenge assumptions, and translate complex business problems into clear recommendations and actions.
Business acumen with financial fluency (NPV, ROI, payback, etc.) to connect project outcomes to enterprise impact.
Strong critical thinking and business judgment, with the ability to ask incisive questions, and influence decisions without direct authority.

Language skills: English
Certifications: Project Management Professional (PMP) Certification and/or Disciplined Agile Scrum Master (DASM) Certification, both granted by Project Management Institute (PMI).
3 - 5 years of experience in Consumer/Durable Goods Sector Product Development. Experience in the Home Appliance industry.

jobs.title: Application Security Program Manager I-II (On-Site)
jobs.description:
Position Function:

The Application Security Program Manager is responsible for leading, governing, and continuously maturing the bank’s application security, identity management, fraud-related technology risk, and emerging technology risk programs within the Information Security Program. This role establishes the strategic direction, operating model, standards, risk assessment methodology, reporting, and multi-year roadmap needed to identity, assess, govern, and reduce risk across application environments.

This position has enterprise scope spanning internally developed applications, third-party hosted solutions, identity platforms, access administration processes, and critical business technologies that support customer-facing and internal operations. This role serves as a senior risk and control leader who partners across Technology, Digital Banking, Fraud, Enterprise Risk, Compliance, Internal Audit, Vendor Management, and other business leadership to align security requirements with business objectives and regulatory expectations.

They will serve as the bank’s senior Subject Matter Expert (SME) in areas related to application security controls, integrations, identity controls, fraud-enabling technology threats, and the security implications of emerging technologies. The role is accountable to lead risk assessments, defining treatment plans, overseeing control effectiveness, and reporting risk posture/key metrics, and advising on enterprise decisions.

The ideal candidate will have broad experience in technology, information security, risk management, securing applications, APIs, identity management, etc. They will work closely with the business and project teams to advocate security requirements to ensure applications and related security practices align with policies, standards, and best practices, while ensuring the security architecture and practices do not infringe on the needs of the business. The position requires taking initiative to research, resource, and be self-reliant when approaching projects and tasks, in addition to being an effective communicator.

They will be responsible for:

Developing and maintaining information security risk management processes that are clear and understandable, workable, up-to-date, and reflect regulatory and CPB-specific requirements and issues.
Assisting in communicating such processes throughout the business, including holding training sessions where appropriate.
Assisting with the planning, coordination, implementation, and management of security measures that manage risks to systems. and data, to prevent unauthorized modification, destruction, or disclosure of information, including outsider service providers.
Analyzing and appraising new products and/or systems for security weaknesses and provide measures to prevent exposure and loss.

Performs all duties and interacts with internal and external customers in a manner aligned with the Company's Core Values of Voyaging Spirit and Positively Ohana; Customer Experience Competencies of Customer Interaction, Empowerment and Ownership; and Basic Skills of Listening, Oral Communication, Written Communication, Action Orientated, Thoroughness, Problem Solving.

Primary Accountabilities:

Responsible for training staff on policies and standards related to application security and identity management best practices, and training staff on methodologies in conducting risk assessments related to this area.
Reviews/delegates work related to the governance and oversight of controls related to application security and identity management.
Leads and motivates a team to ensure high levels of engagement, performance, and productivity.
Sets clear goals and expectations for team members and provides guidance on how to achieve them.
Conducts regular performance reviews to assess individual progress and provide constructive feedback.
Identifies skills gaps and provides opportunities for professional growth through training, mentorship, or cross-functional collaboration.
Leads a risk-based application security review program to ensure appropriate security controls are designed, implemented, and operate effectively.
Validating application and other reference architectures for security best practices, and recommending changes to enhance security and reduce risk where applicable.
Overseeing application risk assessments and control reviews to identify weaknesses and drives remediation plans with accountable stakeholders
Leads security risk evaluation for emerging technologies, new business initiatives, and material changes to the application and identity ecosystem.
Conducting or facilitating threat modeling of services and applications that tie to the risk and data associated with the application or services.
Delivers operational security duties to include, but not limited to:
Providing strategic oversight for application security tooling, processes and service models to support scalable coverage, risk visibility, and business enablement.
Conducting incident response exercises with colleagues throughout the organization and incorporating lessons-learned into existing security architectures and practices.
Conducting forensic analysis of security-related incidents in a manner consistent with best practices and the organization’s counsel.
Other departmental duties and functions include, but not limited to:
Performing risk analyses pertaining to the security needs of the bank and preparing recommendations based on risk/exposure versus cost. Prepares and presents research findings in written and/or oral form. Presents objectives, alternatives, risk analyses, and cost/benefit analyses.
Assists with the planning and directing of information security activities of the bank to ensure compliance with internal/external audits, and to federal and State regulations, which include FDIC, relevant sections of the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act (GLBA), and Sarbanes-Oxley Act Section 404 provisions, and other duties to be assigned.
Maintains an outward-facing and forward-looking view to provide solutions to ensure that the bank’s Information Security Program is current and relevant.
Designs, implements, and manages Information Security data identification, aggregation, analytics, and validation to meet department goals.
Collaborates in developing and maintaining application security documentation (policies, standards, procedures, templates, etc.) that may be applied towards security governance in projects and operations:
Initiates and executes on process improvements, policy/procedure updates, etc.
Tracks developments and changes in the digital banking and threat environments to ensure they are adequately addressed in security strategy plans.
Documents data flows of sensitive information within the organization (e.g., PII or ePHI) and recommends controls to ensure this data is adequately secured (e.g., encryption, tokenization, etc.).
Serves as the Subject Matter Expert in providing guidance in the areas of application security, identity management, and API security:
Participates in application and related infrastructure projects to provide security planning consulting.
Partners with cross-functional teams to ensure security requirements are incorporated into processes and operations.
Liaisons with the vendor management team to conduct security assessments of existing and prospective vendors, especially those with which the organization shares intellectual property, PII, ePHI, regulated or other protected data, including SaaS providers, cloud/infrastructure as a service (IaaS) providers, managed service providers, etc.
Program Manager Responsibilities:
Owns the bank’s application security, identity governance, and fraud-related technology risk programs, and is accountable for strategy, governance, maturity, and measurable risk outcomes.
Establishes program objectives, control standards, operating procedures, risk tolerances, and performance metrics to ensure program effectiveness and regulatory alignment.
Develops and maintains multi-year roadmap for people, process, and technology capabilities, including investment priorities, control enhancements, and maturity targets.
Provides leadership reporting and risk insights to Information Security leadership, executive stakeholders, governance committees, auditors, regulators, and others as appropriate.

Minimum Qualifications:

Education:

Bachelor’s Degree from a 4-year university required, preferably in Information Security, MIS, Computer Science

Experience:

Application Security Program Manager I:

7+ years of experience and working knowledge in information security, application security, and regulations and privacy laws pertaining to release of information, and security and access control technologies, or equivalent experience required
3+ years of experience in management or as a team lead with enterprise-wide cross-functional leadership responsibilities required
1+ years of experience in financial services preferred

1+ years of experience with identity governance and administration platforms and solutions preferred

The Security Manager will provide overall direction, coordination, and guidance for the security program on a project. Directs the development and implementation of security criteria and programs and procedures; provides functional guidance and direction to assigned security personnel and contractors; and monitors security activities and the performance of security services.

Leads the project security program across project site and offices supporting a large, complex, low-to-medium risk construction environment within a commercial/residential setting or industrial park. Establishes security objectives and performance metrics (KPIs) to monitor program effectiveness.

Provides security support and coordination with project disciplines that include but are not limited to Labor/Industrial Relations, Human Resources, Transportation & Logistics, and ES&H to address overlapping risks, promote consistent application of policies, and support safe and compliant project operations.

Formal, specialized training in security, criminal justice, military, or related disciplines.

Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to effectively engage leadership, contractors, clients, and external stakeholders.

Role- SAP BRIM Project Manager

Location- San Jose, CA

Duration: Long Term

Position
Overview We are looking for an experienced SAP BRIM Project Manager / Support Lead to manage our production support, continuous enhancement, and operational governance across the SAP BRIM (Billing and Revenue Innovation Management) landscape. This role combines hands-on functional understanding of core BRIM pillars with project management discipline. You will lead a blended onshore/offshore team, enforce ITIL-based SLA/KPI targets, drive critical incident resolution, and govern small-to-medium business enhancements from scoping to hypercare.

Key Responsibilities

1. Support Operations & SLA Governance Lead day-to-day operations for Level 2 and Level 3 production support across the entire SAP BRIM suite. Own and report operational KPIs: mean time to acknowledge (MTTA), mean time to resolve (MTTR), SLA compliance (>98%), ticket backlog trends, and first-time-fix rates. Serve as the primary escalation point for Priority 1/2 billing, mediation, rating, and invoicing incidents; lead root cause analyses (RCA) and post-mortem discussions. Manage high-volume recurring operations: month-end billing cycles, automated rating batches, bill-run failures, out-of-sequence consumption data, and financial posting reconciliations.
2. Project Management & Continuous Improvement Manage minor release cadences, change requests (CRs), and platform enhancements using hybrid Agile/Scrum or Waterfall frameworks. Own project schedules, resource allocations, sprint backlogs, risk/issues/assumptions/dependencies (RAID) logs, and release readiness checklists. Coordinate end-to-end delivery: requirement discovery, solution design review, build, system integration testing (SIT), regression testing, cutover, and post-deployment stabilization. Interface directly with business finance, IT steering committees, external System Integrators (SIs), and vendor partners.
3. Functional Oversight & Solution Integrity Provide functional governance across core modules: SAP SOM (Subscription Order Management): Subscription lifecycle, master agreements, product catalog, provider contracts. SAP CC (Convergent Charging): Rating and charging logic, charge plans, allowance logic, subscriber mapping. SAP CI (Convergent Invoicing): Billable items (BITs), consumption items (CITs), bill runs, aggregation, invoicing rules. SAP RAR: Revenue postings, reconciliation & rev-rec. Coordinate integration integrity with SAP S/4HANA Finance, SAP CPQ, SAP Integration Suite (CPI), external CRM, and data mediation layers.

Required Qualifications & Experience Total Experience:

8+ years of IT delivery/support experience, with at least 4+ years dedicated to SAP BRIM (formerly Hybris Billing) and 3+ years running project management or application maintenance services (AMS).
Core Technical Expertise: Functional or technical depth in at least two of the four BRIM components (SOM, CC, CI, RAR) alongside familiarity with the overall end-to-end data pipeline.
Support Frameworks: Proven experience running structured ITIL processes (Incident, Problem, Change, and Release Management) using tools such as ServiceNow, Jira, or SAP Solution Manager.

Project Delivery:
Demonstrated success managing cross-functional technical teams (developers, functional consultants, BASIS, middleware teams) across distributed time zones. Integration Acumen: Familiarity with modern SAP interface technologies (OData, REST APIs, IDocs, SAP CPI) and reconciliation between rated events and general ledger entries.

Education: Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, Finance, or a related discipline.

The Business Intelligence Analyst serves as a strategic partner to FP&A, business leaders, and IT, translating financial, operational, and strategic business needs into scalable reporting, analytics, and business intelligence solutions. This role combines strong technical expertise with financial and business acumen to improve data accessibility, reporting capabilities, operational efficiency, and decision support across the organization. The Business Intelligence Analyst partners closely with FP&A, business leaders, and the data warehouse team to transform complex financial and operational data into trusted insights that support informed business decisions.

Position Information

Primary Work Location: Fargo, ND or St. Louis Park, MN
Work Environment: On-Site
Work Type: Full-time, Exempt

Responsibilities

Finance and Business Partnership

Partner with Finance, FP&A, business leaders, and IT to understand reporting, planning, forecasting, and analytics needs and develop practical solutions that support business goals.
Lead conversations with stakeholders to understand business needs, current processes, challenges, data sources, and desired outcomes.
Translate business needs into clear requirements, process documentation, report specifications, and prioritized projects.
Manage and prioritize reporting and analytics requests, balancing ongoing reporting, strategic projects, data quality, and ad hoc needs.
Develop a strong understanding of business systems and processes to identify gaps, clarify responsibilities, and recommend improvements.

Business Intelligence, Reporting, and Analytics

Design, develop, maintain, and improve Power BI dashboards, reports, scorecards, and analytical tools for executive and operational audiences.
Analyze financial and operational data to identify trends, variances, risks, opportunities, and performance drivers, and communicate insights clearly.
Establish consistent reporting definitions, calculations, measures, and business rules while reducing manual reporting, consolidating duplicate reports, and increasing automation and self-service capabilities.
Use advanced Excel capabilities for analysis, reconciliation, forecasting, scenario modeling, and business reporting.
Support self-service reporting by creating reliable datasets, reusable report templates, clear documentation, and user guidance.

Data Modeling and Technical Development

Develop and maintain Power BI semantic models using dimensional-modeling principles, well-defined relationships, measures, dimensions, and hierarchies.
Use SQL, DAX, and Power Query to query, validate, transform, and analyze data.
Leverage Microsoft Fabric and related Microsoft data tools to support reporting and analytical solutions.
Partner with technical resources to ensure reporting requirements are reflected in data models, transformations, and reporting structures.
Support appropriate data security, access controls, and report performance optimization.

Data Warehouse and Systems Integration

Partner with IT, data engineering resources, external consultants, and business stakeholders to define data requirements and improve data integration, automation, and accessibility.
Understand how financial and operational data flows across source systems, Rayfin, data warehouse layers, semantic models, and reporting solutions.
Participate in testing and validation of data pipelines, integrations, and reporting outputs and maintain documentation of KPI definitions, business rules, data sources, and reporting logic.

Data Quality, Governance, and Continuous Improvement

Monitor and resolve data quality, reconciliation, access, performance, and reporting issues in partnership with appropriate stakeholders.
Drive continuous improvement by automating manual processes, simplifying analysis, improving reporting efficiency, and expanding access to trusted information.
Develop and execute testing, coordinate user acceptance testing, and reconcile reporting to source systems and approved business totals.
Document report purpose, data sources, definitions, assumptions, business rules, and ownership to support consistency and long-term maintainability.
Train and support business users on Power BI, trusted datasets, report interpretation, and self-service analytics.
Support emerging AI and advanced analytics initiatives by helping define business value, data requirements, validation criteria, risks, and governance considerations.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Information Systems, Data Analytics, Finance, Accounting, or a related field; equivalent experience may be considered.
3+ years of experience in business intelligence, data analysis, financial analysis, reporting, business analysis, or a related field.
Experience with Microsoft Fabric, OneLake, Fabric Data Warehouse, Lakehouse, Data Factory, or related Microsoft cloud analytics capabilities.
Hands-on experience developing Power BI reports and semantic models using DAX and Power Query.
Working proficiency with SQL for data analysis, reconciliation, testing, and validation.
Experience gathering and documenting business requirements and translating them into reporting, analytics, or process-improvement solutions.
Experience with dimensional data modeling, KPI development, data visualization, data quality, and user acceptance testing.
Working knowledge of financial and operational reporting, including budgeting, forecasting, variance analysis, and performance metrics.
Ability to communicate complex data and technical concepts clearly to both business and technical audiences.
Ability to lead requirements discovery, clarify ambiguous requests, define KPIs and business rules, and establish measurable acceptance criteria.

Our team is made up of operators, marketers, and builders focused on products consumers actually trust. We're investing heavily in data and AI to sharpen how we develop products and scale brands.

About the Role

We are looking for a Senior Data Analyst who is far more than a report builder. You are a "Data Detective" who understands the heartbeat of an e-commerce P&L, and where it's headed next.

You will own the truth behind our financial numbers and how we forecast them. We need a Financial Modeling Master who can build the forecasts our Finance team plans around, plus the predictive models that make those forecasts sharper, all grounded in rigorously reconciled data.

Additionally, you will act as a critical partner to our Finance team and leadership, bridging the gap between raw transaction data, payment processors, and the financial plan.

What You'll Do

1. Forecasting

Financial Forecasts:
Build and own forecasts for revenue, orders, subscription renewals, and cash by brand and channel.
Scenario Planning:
Develop scenario and sensitivity models that help Finance plan budgets.
Forecast Accuracy:
Track accuracy over time and refine forecasts as the business changes.

2. Predictive Modeling

Customer & SKU-Level Models:
Build, validate, and maintain predictive models, such as subscription renewal and cancellation likelihood, refund and chargeback risk, and SKU-level demand, using statistical and machine learning methods (e.g., logistic regression, survival analysis, gradient boosting).
Sharper Forecasts:
Feed model outputs into revenue and cash forecasts so projections reflect who is likely to renew, cancel, or refund, not just historical trends.
Model Health:
Monitor model performance over time and retrain as customer behavior shifts.

3. Financial Reporting & Unit Economics

P&L Reporting:
Own reporting on revenue, gross vs. net sales, discounts, refunds, COGS, and contribution margin by brand, channel, and product.
Unit Economics:
Own contribution margin, payback, and profitability reporting by brand, channel, and product.
Variance Analysis:
Produce budget-vs-actual analysis that explains what moved and why.

4. Financial Data Integrity & Reconciliation

Reconciliation Ownership:
Own reconciliation across payment processors ( Stripe, Shopify Payments, Amazon
), bank deposits, our internal database, and accounting ( QuickBooks
) to ensure every dollar is accounted for.
Root Cause Leadership:

Single Source of Truth:
Define and document the business logic behind financial metrics for the whole company.

Data Preparation:
Use dbt
or Python
to build the financial datasets and models behind forecasting and reporting.
Business Logic Application:
Write efficient SQL in Snowflake
that reflects our financial business rules.
Dashboarding:
Design, build, and maintain high-impact dashboards in Sigma
for Finance and executive leadership.

6. Leadership & Collaboration

Finance Partnership:
Present forecasts and model findings to Finance and executive leadership, including the assumptions and risks behind them.
Raise the Bar:
Review other analysts' work and mentor them on financial data quality and modeling.

What We're Looking For

The Essentials (Experience & Tech Stack)

5+ years of data or financial analytics experience, with meaningful time in DTC, subscription, or consumer businesses. (We are looking for a senior, hands-on individual contributor, not a people manager.)

strong grasp of accounting principles, and familiarity with compiling financial statements and cash flows.

is required. You must be comfortable with Shopify

data.

jobs.title: Data Analyst, Finance
jobs.description:
About Scale

For the past 12 years, Scale Media has been building and scaling science-backed wellness brands. Our portfolio of brands, including Live Conscious, 1MD, and Essential Elements, has grown to 9 figures in revenue while operating profitably with no external funding.

Our team is made up of operators, marketers, and builders focused on products consumers actually trust. We're investing heavily in data and AI to sharpen how we develop products and scale brands.

We believe the best decisions come from data, curiosity, and continuous learning. We value high ownership, candid feedback, and thoughtful execution. As a fully remote company, we lead with clear communication, accountability, and trust, and we give people real room to grow and make an impact.

Scale Media has been recognized as one of Forbes' Best Startup Employers, a Great Place to Work, an Inc. Best Workplace, and an Inc. 5000 company.

If you take ownership, think for yourself, and like solving hard problems alongside people who do the same, you'll fit right in.

About the Role

We are looking for a mid-level Data Analyst who is far more than a report builder. You are a "Data Detective" who understands the heartbeat of an e-commerce P&L.

You will not just analyze data; you will own the truth behind our revenue numbers and help Finance see what's coming next. We need a Financial Data Master who understands payment processors, core financial concepts, and forecasting, and who knows how raw transaction data becomes a P&L the business can trust.

Additionally, you will act as a critical partner to our Finance team, bridging the gap between raw data, payment processors, our financial reporting, and the forecast.

What You'll Do

1. Forecasting

Financial Forecasts:
Build and maintain forecasts for revenue, orders, subscription renewals, and expenses by brand and channel, and keep them current as actuals come in.
Forecast vs. Actual:
Track how forecasts compare to actuals, explain the gaps, and flag meaningful misses to the Finance team.
Budget Support:
Update the scenarios and assumptions Finance uses for budget planning.

2. Financial Reporting & Unit Economics

P&L Reporting:
Build and maintain reporting on revenue, gross vs. net sales, discounts, refunds, COGS, and contribution margin by brand, channel, and product.
Unit Economics:
Report on contribution margin, payback, and profitability by brand, channel, and product.
Month-End Close:
Support month-end close with timely, tied-out data.
Budget vs. Actual:
Produce variance reporting that explains what moved and why.

3. Financial Data Integrity & Reconciliation

Reconciliation Investigations:
Act as the lead investigator for revenue discrepancies. You will reconcile data between payment processors ( Stripe, Shopify Payments, Amazon
), bank deposits, our internal database, and accounting ( QuickBooks
) to ensure every dollar is accounted for.
Spend Reconciliation:
Reconcile marketing spend across ad platforms and invoices against finance records.
Root Cause Fixes:
Work with Finance and our Data Engineer to fix discrepancies at the source.
Metric Definitions:
Document the business logic behind financial metrics so every team uses the same definitions.

4. Data Transformation & Visualization

Data Preparation:
While we have a Data Engineer managing the infrastructure, you will handle the "last mile" of data prep using KNIME
or dbt
(or similar tools like Alteryx or Python/Pandas).
Business Logic Application:
Write efficient SQL to transform raw transaction data in Snowflake
into usable datasets that reflect our financial business rules.
Dashboarding:
Design, build, and maintain high-impact dashboards in Sigma
for Finance and leadership.

What We're Looking For

The Essentials (Experience & Tech Stack)

Experience Level:
2–3 years of specific Data Analysis experience, ideally supporting finance. (We are not looking for Junior Analysts or Senior Data Architects; we need a hands-on mid-level executor.)
Forecasting:
Hands-on experience building and maintaining financial forecasts (e.g., revenue, orders, or expenses) in SQL, spreadsheets, or a BI tool. This is required.
Financial Acumen:
Comfort with revenue recognition, COGS, gross vs. net sales, and contribution margin.
Industry:
Proven experience in DTC E-commerce
is required. You must be comfortable with Shopify
, Amazon Seller Central
, and Stripe
data.
Warehousing & BI:
Strong proficiency with Snowflake
(SQL) and Sigma
. We're open to candidates experienced with Tableau, Looker, or Power BI who can adapt quickly.
Spreadsheets:
Advanced Excel or Google Sheets skills.
Transformation Tools:
Competency in KNIME
or dbt
is preferred, but we are open to candidates experienced with Alteryx
or Python
who can adapt quickly.
ELT Familiarity:
Awareness of how ELT tools (like Hevo, Fivetran, Airbyte, Azure
, etc.) function, so you can communicate effectively with our Data Engineer.

The "Financial Data Master" Skill Set

You have built or maintained forecasts that Finance relied on, and you can explain why actuals came in above or below them.
You understand how a Shopify order becomes a processor payout and then a bank deposit, and where fees, refunds, and chargebacks create gaps.
Understanding QuickBooks
report structures is a plus.

The Financial Mindset

You have the patience and precision to trace a single transaction through the entire data lifecycle to solve revenue mismatches.
You'd rather be right than fast, but you're fast too.

What We Offer

Salary: $80,000 - $100,000 depending on experience
Excellent Medical, Dental, Vision and Life insurance
Fully remote, full-time position
Monthly WFH stipend
Generous Paid Time Off program
Discounted Products
An amazing team to work alongside

Provide first-level support in the delivery of high-quality BI reports and services, with a focus on data analysis and data visualization for ad hoc and standardized reporting.

Identify and recommend improvements to data collection, transformation, and analysis processes to enhance data quality, accuracy, and usability.
Support change management activities for new or enhanced BI solutions, including stakeholder communications, user training, hypercare support and tracking of adoption and usage metrics.
Deliver demos, create user guides, and capture user feedback to continuously improve BI solutions and user experience.
Comfortable writing or reviewing basic SQL to validate logic and data

A strong understanding of Agile methodologies and processes

Good to excellent English language communication skills both oral and written

Department Information
Are you interested in making a difference in the lives of fellow Californians while achieving your career goals? Do you set high standards for yourself and enjoy a collaborative and challenging work environment? The mission of the California Department of Social Services is to serve, protect, and support the people of California experiencing need in ways that empower wellbeing and disrupt systemic inequities. The vision of the California Department of Social Services is to provide quality services with a commitment to an inclusive, diverse, and equitable California where all people can thrive.

CDSS Guiding Principles

Diversity. Equity. Inclusion. Accessibility. Belonging.

We ensure opportunities for everyone to participate in a meaningful way in fulfilling the mission and vision of CDSS.

Community Engagement

We prioritize the lived experiences of community members as a driving force behind the creation, implementation, desired impact, or change of programs and services.

Empowerment

We engage, operate, and advocate from the understanding that each community and person has desires and capabilities to lead in their own life.

Quality Services

We provide services that align intent and impact by ensuring that they are accessible, community driven, interconnected, and continuously improved.

Data Defined Outcomes

We equitably collect and analyze data, take data-driven action, and measure outcomes relevant to those we serve, ensuring transparency and accountability.

Job Description And Duties
Do you have strong technical skills in research and data analysis? Are you interested in making a meaningful impact on the lives children and families across California? If so, consider joining the Fiscal Forecasting Branch (FFB) at the California Department of Social Services (CDSS) as a Research Data Analyst (RDA) II, also considering RDA I. This position is part of a dynamic team that is dedicated to serving, aiding and protecting children and adults in ways that strengthen and preserve families, encourage personal responsibility and foster independence. We are looking for a highly motivated Research Data Analyst I/II (RDA I/II) with strong analytical skills who enjoys working in a fast-paced environment to join the Children’s Estimates Unit of the Fiscal Forecasting Branch (FFB) team. The Children’s Estimates Unit develops the annual Local Assistance Governor’s Budget and May Revision update for Children’s programs administered by the County Welfare Departments. In addition, the FFB is responsible for providing a fiscal analysis of proposed legislative bills that have a potential impact to the Department.

The RDA II’s serve as a senior analysts that working with minimal direction, while the RDA I supports complex analysis under general direction. It is essential for the RDA I/II to possess strong analytical skills to conceptualize, develop, and create fiscal estimates that are robust and consider multiple variables (e.g., funding environment, political considerations, data integration). The work intersects with multiple branches across the department and the RDA I/II needs to develop strong working relationships to be successful. The work produced is highly visible and will be scrutinized closely by senior management, executive staff, and external stakeholders because it will have direct implications for the State Budget.

It is desirable that the RDA I/II have an understanding of social service programs’ policies and experience in interpreting and applying statutes, regulations, and following procedures. Additionally, the RDA I/II must be able to work independently, reason logically, and possess strong analytical skills. The RDA I/II is expected to mentor junior staff members, take a lead role in complex assignments, and work as an acting manager when required.

jobs.description:
Job Number: R0250809

All-Source Intelligence Analyst

The Opportunity:

With all of the information available today, it takes a skilled all-source analyst to know how to find and interpret the best data to give their clients the right answers. With the critical decisions made in our government and military every day, we need an intelligence analyst like you to do just that. As a defense industries all-source analyst, you use your specialized functional experience and your attention to detail to conduct all-source analytic production on foreign defense industrial programs, infrastructure, and capabilities supporting a foreign country’s ability to develop, equip, sustain, and employ its military forces across basic, strategic, and military industrial sectors.

As a Defense Industries All-Source Analyst on our team, you’ll help your client by providing intelligence production and briefing support to address dynamic intelligence requirements. Using your comprehensive understanding of all-source analytic tradecraft, production cycles, publication standards, community writing styles, and formats, you’ll produce strategic-level assessments and products that address the research, development, acquisition, test, evaluation and production of foreign weapon systems and equipment. As an authority on your topic, your client will look to you for comprehensive production, often under pressure.

This is a chance to grow your expertise and broaden your skill set in areas like analysis, writing, and communication. You’ll share your expertise with other analysts through leadership and mentoring. We focus on growing as a team to deliver the best support to our customers, so you’ll have resources to learn new skills and tools. Join us as we provide the right information at the right time to support the critical needs of our warfighters and nation’s leaders.

Join us. The world can’t wait.

You Have:

Knowledge of IC and Combatant Command environments
Ability to develop high-quality deliverables tailored to senior policymakers or defense stakeholders, including complex written products and formal or informal briefings
TS/SCI clearance
Bachelor's degree and 3+ years of experience in all-source analysis, or 7+ years of experience in all-source analysis in lieu of a degree

Nice If You Have:

3+ years of experience with defense industries analysis such as industrial organization, production processes, foreign weapon systems and equipment, and their associated facilities and output levels
Knowledge of ICD 203 and 206 analytic tradecraft standards
Knowledge of the INDOPACOM AOR

Clearance:

Applicants selected will be subject to a security investigation and may need to meet eligibility requirements for access to classified information; TS/SCI clearance is required.

Evaluate high-priority assets across the portfolio and recommend actions to maximize returns or mitigate risks.

Ensure that Real Estate management and senior executives have access to reliable, comprehensive, and timely data.

jobs.title: Greenhouse Program Manager
jobs.description:
The Horticultural Society of New York (The Hort) seeks a creative and strategic Greenhouse Program Manager to lead educational programming, community engagement, and public events at the Greenhouse and Education Center at Denny Farrell Riverbank State Park. Reporting to the Director of the Greenhouse and Education Center and with the support of GPSWFs, the Greenhouse Program Manager will be responsible for the implementation of a diverse portfolio of horticulture-based educational experiences serving children, families, educators, older adults, workforce development participants, and community members. This individual will position the Greenhouse and Education Center as a vibrant destination for learning, wellness, environmental stewardship, and community connection.

The Horticultural Society of New York brings plants into the places where daily life happens, especially in neighborhoods with the least access to green space. We turn “unplantable” urban spaces—sidewalks, medians, traffic triangles, and streets—into gardens and plantings that last. We engage communities through learning, wellness, and paid work, so the benefits of plants are more accessible to New Yorkers across our city.

Responsibilities

Program Leadership & Curriculum Implementation

Implement, and oversee educational programming for diverse audiences.
Administer directly and support others in delivering The Hort’s seasonal and year-round curricula rooted in horticulture, environmental education, food growing, and community stewardship.
Ensure internal and externally facilitated programming that aligns with The Hort's mission and strategic priorities.
Evaluate and continuously improve program quality and participant outcomes.

Daily operations and scheduling

Serve as the point of contact person on-site across assigned shifts, including opening and closing.
Resolve front-line problems and maintain a safe, orderly, welcoming site.
Prepare spaces, materials, and setups for booked programs and guest-facilitated sessions.
Coordinate the weekly scheduling of staff assigned to the Greenhouse.
Support all program logistics, including space, scheduling, and daily presence.

Program Management & Staff Supervision

Supervise educators, facilitators, and interns assigned to work at the Greenhouse
Provide coaching, training, and professional development opportunities.
Ensure program delivery is consistent, inclusive, and high quality.

Events & Public Programming

Lead plant-focused community events, seasonal celebrations, workshops, exhibitions, and open houses.
Coordinate logistics with operations staff and external partners.
Support fundraising and donor engagement events held at the site.

Evaluation, Grants & Administration

Support tracking participation metrics and program outcomes.
Prepare reports for grants, funders, and organizational leadership.
Assist with program budgets and strategic planning.
Other tasks, as directed

Qualifications

Experience managing program delivery and front-line staff, ideally at a community, education, or public-facing site.
2+years of experience managing educational or community programs.
Experience delivering curriculum and facilitating learning for diverse audiences.
Strong operational skills for scheduling and staff management.
Familiarity with horticulture, gardening, urban agriculture, or environmental education preferred.

Preferred Qualifications

Bilingual (Spanish/ English)
Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite (Outlook, Word, Excel, PPT, etc.)

Physical Requirements

Able to lift 50+ pounds and comfortable working outside in all weather conditions.
Ability to squat, lift, stretch, bend, sit and stand for extended periods of time
Ability to perform physical labor outside in all weather conditions.
Comfort navigating the subway, bus, streets, and other modes of transportation throughout NYC

Benefits

The Hort offers all Full-Time regular employees a generous Paid Time Off package, term life insurance policy, and Employee Assistance Program. Pre-tax benefits include transit, Flexible Spending Account, medical, dental, and vision insurance. A 401(k)-retirement plan is available after one year of service.

Additional Details

Schedule: Sunday-Thursday 10am-6pm
Work Locations: Denny Farrell Riverbank State Park Greenhouse and Education Center, and other approved locations
Reports to: Director, Greenhouse and Education Center
Salary: 66,300-68,000 annual salary
Background Check: Facilitators may be screened by the DOE Office of Personnel Investigation and submit fingerprints

How To Apply

Please include a brief cover letter detailing your interests along with the completed application and resume. To be considered, click here to submit your application and required materials. Only complete applications will be reviewed. No phone calls.

Please be advised that due to the high volume of applicants, we can only contact candidates whose skills and background best fit the open positions' needs. Thank you for your interest in employment opportunities at The Horticultural Society of New York.

Managed & Professional Services

Full-Time
United Kingdom

Build Your Future With Us

The digitization of tax compliance is fundamentally changing global commerce and how businesses need to operate and grow. Governments now have real-time visibility into business data, creating new challenges and new opportunities for organizations around the world. At Sovos, we're transforming tax compliance from a business requirement into a driver of growth through AI-powered technology that delivers the accurate, real-time insights businesses need to make smarter decisions.

We're solving more than today's tax compliance challenges. We're helping reshape global economies by enabling organizations to navigate increasingly complex and rapidly changing regulatory environments with confidence – and helping communities thrive.

AI is accelerating what's possible, enabling tax and technology professionals to more effectively drive critical regulatory decisions. That's where Sovos excels, combining intelligent technology with human expertise to help customers stay ahead of change.

Don't worry if you don't check every box. We're focused on hiring great people, not perfect resumes. It's less about what you've done elsewhere and more about what you're capable of doing here.

The Role

At Sovos, we're building the future of tax compliance technology across Europe. We're looking for a Senior Project Manager to join our European Professional Services team, with the ability to be based in the United Kingdom, Netherlands, or Spain. This is a senior delivery role for someone who understands the complexity of enterprise SaaS implementations and brings deep familiarity with tax compliance, e-invoicing, or regulatory technology. new_jobs.description:
Scope of Position

About Us

EDF power solutions North America has been providing clean energy solutions throughout the U.S., Canada, and Mexico since 1987. We are a market-leading independent power producer and service provider, serving utilities, corporations, industries, communities, institutions, and investors with reliable, low-carbon energy solutions that help meet growing demand.

From developing and building scalable wind (onshore and offshore), solar, storage (battery and pumped storage hydro), smart EV charging, microgrids, green hydrogen, and transmission projects, to maximizing performance and profitability through skilled operations and maintenance and innovative asset optimization, our teams deliver expert solutions along the entire value chain—from origination to commercial operation.

Be a part of an innovative and collaborative team environment that fosters our goal of delivering renewable solutions to lead the transition to a sustainable energy future.

Benefits & Perks

EDF power solutions offers best-in-class employee benefits, including the following:

Competitive bonus incentives. This position is eligible for our annual bonus program.
Comprehensive health coverage. We provide low-cost health & wellness coverage for employees and their eligible dependents.
Rewarding 401k. We provide a generous matching contribution.

We Are Also Proud To Offer

Favorable paid time off programs, including paid parental leave after one year of service.
Rewarding learning & career development and advancement opportunities.
Supportive mentorship & buddy programs.

Salary Range
:
The full pay range for this role is $107,200 to $178,600 annually, and the good faith estimated starting pay for this position upon hire is $128,610 to $150,045 annually. We generally base our salary decisions on factors including but not limited to, relevant work and leadership experience, education, demonstrated performance, internal equity, and in some cases, geographic location.

Scope of Job
:
Under the direction of the Senior Project Manager or Associate/Director - Project Management, the Project Manager is responsible for managing all aspects and phases of multiple solar EPC projects and programs simultaneously. The Project Manager is primarily responsible for collaboration with project stakeholders such as owners, utilities, landowners, municipalities, developers, consultants, subcontractors, and other project partners and internal resources such as engineering and construction professionals. The Project Manager will achieve project and corporate goals which are generally described as follows: project schedule, project scope management, budget performance, quality assurance requirements, and construction safety. The Project Manager will foster a cooperative relationship with project partners, external owners/clients, and internal resources while meeting the company strategic goals and continually messaging the value of the company services to stakeholders. This position has project P&L responsibility.

Responsibilities

Oversee and manage the delivery of multiple Company projects on time, on budget, and in accordance with all applicable health, safety, contract, quality, and legal requirements; coordinate, supervise, and manage project team consisting of internal resources (i.e., Project Engineers, Assistant Project Managers, Project Coordinators, Superintendents, Design Engineers, and Project Administrators) and outside partners such as subcontractors, consultants, clients, utilities, development partners; take direct responsibility for all aspects of project delivery, where necessary; secure subcontractors; lead team in vetting, qualifying, referencing, scoping, price negotiation, and contracting with subcontractors; implement and manage project administration, site safety, and field quality control, including project meetings, document control, submittals, safety and staff planning, quality control, construction team planning and documentation, and other close‑out and commissioning of projects.
Manage budget, expenses, revenue, margin, and schedule for multiple simultaneous projects; track project actual P&L vs. plan on a monthly basis and take corrective action to meet objectives; accurately forecast project revenues, cost, and margins. Manage subcontractor payments and project billings. Create baseline schedule and maintain weekly and monthly project schedule updates in MS Project and/or Primavera.
Implement health and safety along with quality assurance program for each project; manage project compliance with health and safety as well as inspection & test plans, including compliance by company personnel, subcontractors, customers, and others at the project site; assure continuous compliance by project and subcontractors with requirements of all project contracts, subcontracts, applicable laws, and applicable permits; take primary responsibility for understanding and applying federal, state, and local code and regulatory requirements.
Implement and manage processes to secure and maintain required approvals from customers, interconnection providers, and local authorities having jurisdiction (AHJs); assure accurate and timely submittals to customers, interconnection providers, and AHJs.
Support internal origination, development, financing, and engineering teams on project matters, including project pricing, technical design, compliance with site requirements, permitting, and other constraints; perform project diligence, including site reconnaissance, geotech, and investigations; attend AHJ meetings, oversee and provide input on preparation of project design and construction documentation and plans.
Report on projects to internal and external colleagues and project stakeholders; manage project details and update project progress on Company project management platform along with other duties as assigned.

Supervision of Others : Project task level supervision and direction of matrix-based project staff, including Project Engineers, Construction Managers, Project Coordinators, Superintendents, and Project Administrators; as well as supervision of external project subcontractors and vendors.

Working Conditions : Work time will be spent both at project sites (outdoor construction sites) and in an office environment, with use of computers, telephone, and other office equipment. Travel is expected to be 25% of overall work time.

Fiscal Responsibilities : Project Profit/Loss responsibility.

Qualifications

Education/Experience :

BA/BS degree in Construction Management, Engineering, or related discipline required.
5-7+ years progressive experience in construction and/or development, including as a Project Manager, Project Engineer, Assistant Project Manager, Development Engineer, or Project Superintendent.
Prior experience managing community solar and/or utility scale photovoltaic systems of greater than 3-5 MW, and preferably greater than 10 MW. Must have managed multiple community scale solar projects simultaneously.
Experienced in solar interconnects into the utility distribution and/or transmission grids at 12kv or greater.
Advanced understanding of contracts, plans, specifications, codes, design/build contracts, and construction means and methods.
Experienced with land development and project financial closing requirements.
Experience with large-scale cut and fill earthwork or landfill construction required.
Experience with subcontracting industrial or large commercial electrical work required.

Skills/Knowledge/Abilities

Strong knowledge of contract language and contract negotiations
Understanding of project cost accounting and tracking procedures
Ability to create and execute project work plans
Strong organizational and time management skills
Ability to work with both internal colleagues and external customers and subcontractors
Strong experience in construction logistics, scheduling, estimating, and budgeting
A commitment to a safe working environment
Ability to adapt easily and accept changing situations
Ability to multi-task and prioritize
Detail orientated
Prior experience utilizing Procore for solar project management, contracting, and quality control.

Physical Requirements : Frequent travel to various North American project sites having varying terrain and weather conditions. Ability to stand and walk for long periods of time. Ability to lift up to 50 pounds on occasion.
